subject: Re: Urgent: PeakCheckout live eventstream garbling — multiple clients impacted
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@peakcheckout.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@peakcheckout.com
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Live: sudden error spike and corrupted eventstream frames

Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp rise in errors around 08:40 PDT across our checkout cluster. Clients using the Redwood client SDK for event streaming are receiving truncated payloads and the stream parser is failing with "unexpected end of headers" and "KV cache mismatch". This began right after your SDK 1.8.3 push on the 17th.

Impact: 12% 5xxs on /v1/live/events in the last 30m, several checkout sessions aborted (see attached tail of error log). We opened a Priority 1 incident on our side (INC-9992) and are looped in. Can you confirm whether you shipped any changes to the streaming dechunker or header reassembly? We need an immediate mitigation — even a temporary fallback to polling would be tolerable while you triage.

Attachments: peak_error_log_tail.txt, sre_handoff_screenshot.png

Claire
SRE Lead, PeakCheckout
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire@peakcheckout.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live: sudden error spike and corrupted eventstream frames

Claire — thanks for the signal and the logs. I'm on it. Initial ask/plan: 

1) Can you forward full ingress traces (request ids) for two failed sessions? That will let us correlate tokenization + headers.
2) I'm pulling the 1.8.3 client SDK release notes and diff now — will confirm any streaming/decoder changes.
3) Temporary mitigation: we can flip a routing policy to route PeakCheckout traffic to a compatibility build (1.8.1) or enable short-polling for the affected endpoints; which do you prefer?

I'm copying Rishi (runtime) and Vanessa (CS exec) for triage and SLA coordination. We'll aim for a hotfix/rollback timeline in the next 4 hours.

— Jonas
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: quick triage — likely client dechunker regression (1.8.3)

Summary of my initial triage: I ran the 1.8.3 dechunker locally against the sample log Claire attached. Observed the same "unexpected end of headers" when frames arrive with a split header boundary across TCP packets plus a specific gzip content-length path we hadn't exercised in CI. There was a refactor in 1.8.3 (commit c3f8b2a) that changed how the parser coalesces trailers; a unit test that used to catch this was accidentally skipped in the release.

Immediate recommended actions: 
- Draft a minimal 1.8.4 hotfix that restores the old coalescing path (I have a spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/clientsdk/pull/812).
- Prepare a canary deploy to a single dedicated pool or route PeakCheckout to 1.8.1 for stability.
- Add a quick health-check to detect header-split errors and failover to polling.

I'll cut the patch and run a small canary in staging by 15:00 PDT. If rollbacks are acceptable to the customer we can do a traffic swap sooner. If this ends up affecting additional accounts we should escalate to Execs for credits/SLA.

Rishi
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire@peakcheckout.com>, PeakCheckout SRE <sre@peakcheckout.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live: sudden error spike and corrupted eventstream frames

Claire / PeakCheckout team —

Thanks for the fast escalation and the traces. We have identified a regression in the 1.8.3 client SDK's streaming dechunker that can mishandle header boundaries in a narrow set of packetization patterns. Rishi has a hotfix PR ready and we can do one of the following immediately: 

Option A (fastest): Route your production traffic to the compatibility build (1.8.1) while we validate the patch. This is a configuration change and should restore stability in ~15 minutes.

Option B: Deploy 1.8.4 hotfix to a canary pool and then promote. Estimated time-to-stable ~90 minutes (tests + canary).

We recommend Option A for immediate risk reduction. If you approve, we'll do the routing swap now and follow with the hotfix deploy.

Operational notes: 
- We'll proactively add an alert to detect header-split parsing errors and fail traffic to polling if detected.
- If this incident causes revenue-impacting outages, Redwood will offer a credit per SLA terms; Vanessa will coordinate commercial remediation.

Please reply with your preferred mitigation and two example request-ids to swap.

— Jonas
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire@peakcheckout.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-18T17:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Live: sudden error spike and corrupted eventstream frames

Claire / team —

I've been briefed and will escalate to CTO and Ops leadership. Jonas / Vanessa: approved to offer up to one week of service credit if the incident is confirmed as caused by our SDK regression. Legal, please standby for any contract exception paperwork.

Jonas — keep me posted on the routing swap outcome. If you need an exec call with PeakCheckout we can join.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
